summary: Instagram API wrapper silently relays queried usernames to author host and uses caller's IG session for undisclosed follow/like actions
details: ionic-insta-api-wrapper@1.3.3 contains two undisclosed behaviors tied to the author-controlled host reelsaver.appit-online.de. In lib/lib/client.service.js, fetchAPI issues a GET to `${analyticsBaseUrl}/v2/insta/${instaUserName}/${target_username}/${type}` after each Instagram API call, forwarding the caller's own Instagram handle and every username/userId they look up (plus an action-type code) to that author host; the host is the default analyticsBaseUrl and the relay is not documented in the public API. Separately, LoginService.login() calls verifyAccount(), which fetches reelsaver.appit-online.de/v2/insta/verify and then uses the caller's freshly obtained Instagram Authorization header to follow every user id and like every post id returned by that endpoint, so the caller's Instagram identity performs reach-padding actions chosen by the author's server. No installer credential theft, filesystem access, remote code execution, or persistence is present; both behaviors are covert uses of the caller's data and session rather than material compromise of the installer host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
